#4251. A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system

For decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder. Now, researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have uncovered evidence that challenges 30 years of established thinking and could open the door to a new treatment.

The condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening. A new study published in Immunity identifies a previously underrecognized problem involving natural killer (NK) cells, immune cells that normally help the body eliminate infected cells.

The researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur. The discovery also points to a possible treatment using existing medications called JAK inhibitors, which could be particularly valuable for patients who do not respond to current therapies.

"This study has revealed a new target for this inflammatory disorder and sets the scene for future clinical studies to explore the use of JAK inhibitors or other drugs to neutralize interferon gamma in patients with MKD," says Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author of the study. "This could lead to a targeted treatment that hasn't been tried before."

Why a Rare Immune Disease Causes Dangerous Inflammation

MKD is a lifelong condition known to affect hundreds of children and adults around the world, although researchers suspect that many people with the disorder have never been diagnosed. Patients experience recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and inflammation in the abdomen. The most serious episodes can cause potentially fatal complications.

For roughly three decades, research into the disease has largely centered on macrophages, immune cells that help coordinate the body's inflammatory defenses. Existing treatments are designed to block an inflammatory signal released by these cells. However, approximately half of patients do not respond adequately, leaving a major need for better treatment options.

To investigate what might be missing from the prevailing explanation, the Garvan team examined blood samples from people with MKD and studied preclinical models of the disorder.

Their experiments revealed a significant defect in natural killer cells, which play an important role in the body's early defenses against viral infections. In MKD, these cells fail to mature properly and struggle to perform one of their most important functions: destroying infected cells before an infection can spread.

The consequences go beyond an impaired ability to fight infection. When natural killer cells cannot eliminate their targets, they release large amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, activating other parts of the immune system and potentially triggering widespread inflammation.

"We found that these immune cells are essentially misfiring," explains Professor Rogers. "NK cells are loaded with toxic ammunition, stored in granules that are released to kill infected cells. However, in MKD these toxic granules can't be released from NK cells and remain trapped inside. When an NK cell fails to kill its target, it compensates by shouting for help, pumping out large amounts of interferon gamma - a powerful inflammatory signal. This activates other immune cells and causes the dangerous fever and widespread inflammation seen in patients."

Discovery Challenges 30 Years of Immune Disease Research

The findings suggest that natural killer cell dysfunction, rather than macrophage activity alone, plays a central role in driving MKD.

Dr. Marcia Munoz, Group Leader in the Rogers Lab and lead researcher on the study, says the results represent a major change in how scientists understand the disease.

"This really turns on its head 30 years of dogma about what was thought to be the underlying mechanism of disease. In MKD, the primary problem is in NK cells and not in macrophages, as previously believed," she says.

To investigate how this cellular defect contributes to the disorder, the Garvan researchers collaborated with Professor Mariapia Degli-Esposti and scientists at Monash University.

Using preclinical models, the team established a connection between malfunctioning natural killer cells and the severe symptoms associated with MKD. Their experiments showed that when the immune system cannot clear a viral infection, the resulting inflammatory response can cause extensive damage to organs.

These results help explain why a disorder involving defective immune defenses can also produce episodes of extreme inflammation.

Existing Drug Shows Promise for a New Treatment

The discovery has already helped guide an experimental treatment approach for a severely affected infant.

Working with doctors at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, the researchers explored whether baricitinib could reduce the excessive inflammatory signaling associated with MKD.

Baricitinib belongs to a class of medications known as JAK inhibitors. These drugs interfere with signaling pathways used by the immune system, including those involved in responses to interferon gamma. The medication is already used to treat other immune-related conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema.

Doctors added baricitinib to the infant's existing treatment regimen and subsequently observed an improvement in the child's condition. Inflammatory flare-ups became less frequent, and severe inflammation affecting the gastrointestinal tract began to heal.

Although the results from a single patient cannot establish whether the treatment will work more broadly, the improvement provides encouraging early evidence for a strategy that targets a different part of the inflammatory process.

The researchers believe their findings provide a foundation for future clinical studies investigating JAK inhibitors and other medications that block interferon gamma activity in patients with MKD, particularly those who have not benefited from standard treatments.

Discovery Could Help Explain Other Genetic Diseases

The potential implications extend beyond MKD itself.

Researchers have introduced the term 'prenylopathies' to describe a family of genetic disorders involving the same metabolic pathway affected in MKD. Early findings suggest that these related diseases may share a similar underlying problem involving natural killer cells that fail to function properly and instead generate excessive inflammatory signals.

If further studies confirm this connection, scientists may be able to identify common disease mechanisms and develop more targeted approaches to diagnosis and treatment across multiple disorders.

"Confirming this link could help end the diagnostic odyssey many patients endure for years or even decades before receiving effective treatment," says Professor Rogers.

Professor Mike Rogers is a Conjoint Professor at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney. Dr. Marcia Munoz is a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney.

#4250. 8 Soulslikes With the Most Unforgiving Checkpoint Systems

Christian Bognar is a Contributor at DualShockers with over three years of experience covering the gaming industry. Since 2022, he has written guides and reviews for publications including DualShockers, CBR, Attack of the Fanboy, PC Invasion, and The Game Slayer. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration

Finding the next checkpoint in any Soulslike game feels like a godsend. After fighting through waves of enemies, gathering a ton of loot and experience points, you’re hopeful that the next checkpoint will come soon so you can level up.

While there are Soulslikes out there that are generally pretty generous when it comes to their checkpoint systems, there are others that are extremely punishing. The more punishing checkpoint systems tend to feel more rewarding, but are also the cause of a lot of frustration.

There are times when a Soulslike can get too difficult out of nowhere. This list covers eight Soulslikes that have insane difficulty spikes.

In this list, we take a look at eight games that have a punishing checkpoint system. Whether it's because their checkpoints are too far apart, levels feature too many enemies, or the runbacks to the bosses are miserable, you will find it in this list.

Demon’s Souls essentially started the idea of including unforgiving checkpoint systems in games. Unlike later FromSoftware games that provide plenty of shortcuts and checkpoints near challenging encounters, Demon’s Souls often forces players to replay lengthy sections of a level.

The Shrine of Storms and Valley of Defilement are two clear examples of this, where the trek between checkpoints, otherwise known as Archstones, is more intimidating than the bosses themselves. Plus, the game’s unique “World Tendency” mechanic, which makes the world more challenging with each death, makes the lack of checkpoints hit even harder.

Lords of the Fallen’s most unique trait is its checkpoint system, which comes in the form of Vestiges. There are permanent Vestiges and Umbral Flowerbeds, temporary Vestiges that players can activate by planting a seed.

While the permanent Vestiges remain at all times, they are extremely far apart in each level, making it so the player has to rely on planting Vestige Seeds into Umbral Flowerbeds. However, this is easier said than done considering Vestige Seeds are generally rare.

Even though Hollow Knight: Silksong is primarily a Metroidvania, and an excellent one at that, it has enough Soulslike elements that make it fit right at home in the genre. And it fits right at home in this list due to its checkpoint system that can be a downright pain in the butt.

Silksong’s checkpoints are rarely near each other. This is especially punishing in a game like Silksong since dying could lead to the player having to repeat a series of platforming challenges. The lack of checkpoints is especially noticeable for some bosses, like The Last Judge and Groal the Great, each with extensive platforming runbacks to the boss arena.

Dark Souls 2’s infamous bonfires aren’t disliked because of their distance from each other, but for the excruciating number of enemies between them. Some gaps between bonfires are littered with too many elite enemies, mobs, traps, and more, making the game sometimes feel like a chore.

The checkpoints are especially punishing when it comes to the game’s bosses, since the bosses are not easy and the runbacks between bonfire and boss arena are excruciatingly long. Having to trek all the way back to the boss arena just to attempt to boss fight again is simply tiring.

It's not the genre's area of expertise, but some of its representatives are more daring, offering fascinating movement mechanics.

Mortal Shell’s checkpoint system is unforgiving for multiple reasons. One, they are generally well-hidden and away from areas worth exploring, and two, Mortal Shell’s level design is filled with interconnecting paths that make it easy to get lost.

Usually in a Soulslike, you lose experience points or resources upon death, such as “Souls” in Dark Souls. However, in Mortal Shell, you lose both Tar and Glimpses, which are two necessary resources for character progression. Losing two important resources instead of one makes finding a checkpoint even more stress-inducing.

The checkpoint system in Bleak Faith: Forsaken is punishing due to the absurdly large environments players will be exploring during a playthrough. Not only are the levels huge, but they are also genuinely confusing, causing players to easily get lost.

Due to the low budget and only a three-person team behind the project, it can sometimes feel like you’re playing a game with no clear direction. This, plus the fact that checkpoints are few and far between, can make it feel like you’re always being punished.

Hellpoint’s checkpoints come in the form of Breaches, and even though they are key to progression, they don’t act like your typical Soulslike checkpoint. For starters, they don’t restore your healing supplies, meaning they can’t be used as a way to survive longer. Players have to instead focus on inventory management for that.

On the other hand, Breaches are scattered throughout large levels, meaning there are tons of enemies between them. Dying in Hellpoint results in dropping Axions, an important resource for leveling, but also spawns a ghost of your past character that you have to fight when returning to the spot of death. This can make reaching the next checkpoint even more difficult than before.

Bloodborne has some notoriously distant checkpoints, especially when compared to other FromSoftware titles and Soulslikes in general. This is punishing enough, but the fact that the game is downright brutal when it comes to the amount of damage enemies deal, distant checkpoints feel even more punishing.

Some examples of a few lamp checkpoints include Nightmare of Mensis and Forbidden Woods, some of the hardest areas in the game that have long stretches of dangerous enemies. Players can expect to die many times in these areas alone before even coming close to the next checkpoint, depending on skill level.

If you're looking for the heir to Soulsborne games, look no further than this list of ten Soulslikes that are unexpected masterpieces.

#4249. Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and important pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.

Research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions. This is because semaglutide acts on the brain to increase the feeling of fullness and to decrease appetite.

These medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however. Our multidisciplinary research team at the University of Alberta is working to improve obesity care for people of all ages and to understand why some people respond better to semaglutide than others, and how their weight loss can be maintained over time.

We are investigating the role of energy metabolism as a potentially important piece in a complex puzzle.

Research has shown semaglutide medications to improve quality of life, blood markers such as sugar or cholesterol, strength and overall health. Weight loss is only one measure of how well they work.

We are exploring whether people’s responses to these medications could lie in individual factors such as genetics, metabolism, body composition, lifestyle, microbiota, associated diseases, age and sex.

Energy metabolism may also be an important piece of this puzzle. This is a measure of the total calories consumed (in) and the total calories burned (out). We burn calories all the time: for vital processes like breathing and thinking, physical activities like going to the gym and the everyday act of digesting food.

When we lose weight, our bodies naturally need less energy. But sometimes, the body goes into an extra “energy-saving mode,” burning even fewer calories than we would expect. This is called metabolic adaptation, or adaptive thermogenesis.

Think of it like a light bulb that automatically dims to save electricity. This is one reason why losing weight can become more difficult over time, sometimes leading to a weight-loss plateau.

Changes in body weight and composition (the amount of fat and fat-free mass in our bodies) play an important role in energy metabolism. Both fat and fat-free mass use energy, even when we are resting. As we lose these tissues, our bodies naturally burn fewer calories.

Researchers are still trying to understand whether weight-loss medications influence these processes differently. If we can understand how our bodies use energy during and after weight loss, this could help us develop better strategies for maintaining weight loss over the long term.

We published a recent review of studies investigating the effects of GLP-1 therapies on energy utilization. We found a few studies exploring how semaglutide affects resting energy use, with findings that were neutral or inconclusive.

The question of how semaglutide impacts energy use is an emerging area of study, and remains an open question for exploration.

At the University of Alberta, we have a gold-standard method to measure energy utilization called a whole-room indirect calorimeter. This is a rare research facility and is similar to a hotel suite that can precisely measure each component of energy use. This room can isolate the effects of changes in someone’s calorie burning at rest, after eating and during exercise.

We are currently recruiting research participants with blood sugar regulation issues, such as insulin resistance or diabetes, who are about to start semaglutide treatment. We will follow their weight loss journey over six months to investigate changes in body weight and composition, and energy utilization using sophisticated approaches.

Understanding how semaglutide influences energy use and body composition, and how these changes interact, could be an important step toward explaining why individuals respond differently to weight-loss treatment.

This will allow us to contribute to more personalized approaches to obesity and Type 2 diabetes management in the future. Having a better understanding of how energy use changes with semaglutide-induced weight loss will also help us to better anticipate potential non-responders (people who do not lose weight) and offer alternative treatments sooner in their health journey.

Importantly, current evidence suggests that if you are taking semaglutide or considering starting treatment, you should make a few lifestyle changes.

#4245. After Much Secrecy, We Finally Have the GTA 6 Cast List

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Prior to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 today, Rockstar had been doing its utmost to play just about every aspect of the game’s production outside of explicitly-revealed details as close to the vest as possible. That’s the whole reason why that little saga of GTA 6 leaks was such a big deal, because so much about the game was in a proverbial black box before launch. Now, though, the game is finally in the world’s collective hands, and that means every little itty-bitty detail is readily-available for everyone to obsessively comb through.

One of those details, and arguably one of the most crucial to the production, is the game’s cast of voice actors. Ahead of the game’s release, the vast majority of the cast was shrouded in mystery, with the single exception being veteran actor Stephen Root revealing his role as Brian Heder, though naturally, that didn’t stop the rampant speculation from the precious few soundbites we got in the trailers.

Now that the game is out, the full cast list has been revealed via the in-game credits, which you technically don’t even need to finish the game to see. Perhaps unsurprisingly for such a high-profile production, many of the game’s voice actors come from TV and film backgrounds, a testament to Rockstar’s star power magnetism.

Rockstar’s latest release has already attracted millions of viewers.

First and foremost, let’s get into our two lead characters, and the most important roles in GTA 6, Jason and Lucia, the duo that had successfully captured hearts and minds before the game was even out. Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke, a television actor who has had a small spattering of roles since 2013, with some standouts including Modern Family, Grey’s Anatomy, Station 19, and In the Vault.

Meanwhile, Lucia, the series's first female protagonist, is voiced by Manni L. Perez, who has previously provided incidental roles in GTA 5 and GTA Online. Outside of games, she’s had a lot of experience in various crime shows, such as The Blacklist, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.

Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke [...] Lucia, meanwhile, is voiced by Manni L. Perez.

Surprisingly, one of the biggest names in the cast aside from the aforementioned Stephen Root is Bobby Moynihan in the role of Jason’s bumbling buddy Cal. Moynihan is a seasoned actor who got his start all the way back in 1996 with roles in live-action and animated film and television like Portlandia, Aqua Teen Hunger Force, and We Bare Bears, though his most decorated gig was various roles on Saturday Night Live since 2008, most notably his recurring character on the “Weekend Update” sketches.

Some other names dropped in the credits include Dre'Quan as Naiqui Macabroad, Orlagh Cassidy as Lori Heder, Brad Carter as Donnie, Mallory Wu as Andy, and rappers Hood Brat and Krissy Celess as Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, respectively. You can check out the credits yourself either by beating the game or just checking the in-game settings menu.

If I were a betting man, I’d put money down on most, if not all of the biggest names in this cast making appearances at The Game Awards next month. In fact, Manni L. Perez has already been nominated for Best Performance as Lucia, among the many, many other categories that GTA 6 has been nominated for alongside Game of the Year.

It’s gonna be a star-studded event, as it often is, of course, but by appearing in the biggest game of the release, quite possibly the entire decade, just about everyone in the GTA 6 cast have just earned some major street cred in the entertainment industry. Obviously, Stephen Root and Bobby Moynihan were already well-established actors, but hopefully, we’ll be seeing a lot more of Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez both in and out of the gaming scene going forward.

You leave a mark like that on entertainment history, and people will start actively seeking you out in every other production you appear in. Hey, maybe they’ll make cameos if we ever get a GTA movie.

Sam Houser offered up a rare statement ahead of what might just be the biggest video game launch in modern history.

T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It said he was starting a new chapter with the organisation.

His record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

His exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It said it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The new deal runs until the end of 2028.

The VCT structure for 2027 was announced on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

#4240. Yakuza Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down, Ending Gang Of Dragon's Development With It

Nagoshi Studio, the developer led by Yakuza/Like a Dragon series creator Toshiro Nagoshi, has officially shut down, ending development of Gang of Dragon, which was revealed at The Game Awards last year. Shareholders resolved to dissolve the studio on October 31, according to a notice published in a Japanese government newspaper called Kanpo, as first reported by Gematsu.

This follows a report from Bloomberg earlier this year that said Chinese gaming megacorp NetEase Games was cutting funding to Nagoshi Studio, allowing Nagoshi to seek independent funding elsewhere. #4237. Interview: Astrae Oratio's game director offers new insights into the upcoming RPG's combat after closed beta

Alongside Limit Zero Breakers, the upcoming RPG Astrae Oratio is arguably the biggest and most interesting launch NCSoft have in the chamber. Set in a world of magic and modernity co-existing side-by-side, it features gorgeous anime-inspired art and interesting gameplay. Or at least the latter is what the Astrae Oratio dev team will hope.

With the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans. With combat being so different to other games on the market, Lim has been eager to demonstrate to fans that their feedback has been heard.

"Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement. We are refining things so that combat can be enjoyed more smoothly by the official launch."

However, Lim was also quick to reiterate exactly why Astrae Oratio's more interactive take on combat, contrary to a popular trend in other games towards auto-battler mechanics, was so important.

"We wanted to capture both the tactile satisfaction of directly controlling your character and the strategic thrill of planning your next move. The starting point for combat in Astrae Oratio was combining the excitement of fighting games, things like reading your opponent’s movements, finding openings, and stringing together combos, with the resource management of turn-based games.

"What connects these is AP, the action resource. By choosing whether to invest in attacks and press the advantage or save it for responding, you find yourself thinking about both moment-to-moment inputs and your next move.

"Ultimately, we want to bring each character’s unique fighting style to life in combat and allow players to gain the advantage using their own judgment and inputs."

Notably, although Lim does defend the original design intent behind how Astrae Oratio will work, he also went into detail on the specific pain points from players that they wanted to address.

"The forced use of specific characters, the disappearance of remaining AP when an enemy is defeated, and the insufficient rewards for successful parries that you mentioned are also important feedback items we identified in that process. The current rules are not set in stone.

"In particular, we plan to rework how leftover AP is handled so the flow of combat isn’t interrupted, and enhance parrying so that landing a successful parry feels genuinely rewarding. We will continue making adjustments based on the feedback from the test and by validating those results moving forward."

All of these are, of course, valid concerns for many fans. But it's clear that the folks behind Astrae Oratio have confidence in their vision for combat. And in truth I can't blame them, as nowadays it seems as though combat is considered a 'solved problem', even where there's room to experiment and tweak.

So, in that regard, it's refreshing to see NCSoft's development team look more closely at what they can do to change things. Although if you are concerned about playing all the time manually and the pressure that it invokes, Lim was quick to point out changes which will make it easier for those wanting a more laid-back experience.

"To preserve the advantages of manual combat, where you make your own judgments and inputs, we plan to maintain a certain degree of efficiency over auto-combat. However, to reduce the fatigue of repeated play, we are improving the pacing of auto-combat and also reviewing additional speed-up options.

"We also plan to significantly expand the limits on boosted play to avoid inconveniencing players, and while it won’t be a traditional sweep mechanic, we are developing a feature that allows you to acquire needed resources more conveniently. We will strive to deliver both the thrill of hands-on combat and the convenience needed for daily grinding."

Overall, it seems as if the closed beta was a success for Astrae Oratio, and even the developers themselves admit that it was exciting to get new feedback from players out in the wild.

"The positive responses to the story and art gave us great encouragement. We also received diverse opinions on what felt fun in the combat system and what needs improvement, and based on this, we will strive to deliver an even more polished version."

And as for how it felt for fans to get their hands on Astrae Oratio from all across the world?

"There were differences in detailed reactions by region, but the way users appreciated the appealing content we intended to present was similar. It gave the sense that there are no borders when it comes to what you love. Indeed, you could say 'when it comes to otaku, we are the world.'" I think that Astrae Oratio is shaping up to be a particularly interesting new entry in NCSoft's catalogue. And while I can never truly forgive them for canning the surprisingly fun little MOBA called Battle Crush, I think that Astrae Oratio and Limit Zero Breakers make for exciting substitutes.

If you want to see what they'll be competing against when Astrae Oratio does launch, well, there's no need to trawl through our back catalogue to find out. Instead, why not dig into our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some of our choice picks?

#4234. Rockstar Is Promoting GTA 6 in a Country Where It Can't Officially Sell It

Rockstar is promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 to players in mainland China, even though the game hasn't been approved for official sale there. It's an unusual situation for one of the biggest launches of the year, but the company's social media activity makes it clear that Chinese players are still part of the audience it's trying to reach.

Rockstar’s latest release has already attracted millions of viewers.

According to a Reuters report published on November 18, Rockstar posted a GTA 6 preorder-related video on Douyin, the Chinese counterpart to TikTok, on November 12. The video encouraged users to preload the game ahead of its worldwide November 19 release.

The Douyin account is verified under Rockstar International Limited and showed a Shanghai IP location when Reuters reviewed it. By November 18, it had attracted around 480,000 followers and more than 300,000 likes. That's a sizeable audience for a game that can't be sold through officially approved channels in mainland China.

The promotion itself isn't complicated. Rockstar was telling fans that GTA 6 was available to preload on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, just as it had been doing for players elsewhere. What's unusual is the market receiving that message.

Reuters was able to access both the account and its promotional video in China. Neither Rockstar nor the National Press and Publication Administration, the country's regulator, had responded to the publication's requests for comment when the report was filed.

This isn't the same as Rockstar announcing an official Chinese release. A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China. The studio also hasn't said that an approved release is on the way.

Imported video games have to pass a government approval process before they can be officially sold in mainland China. The authorities scrutinize content such as violence, sexual material, and politically sensitive themes. Given what Grand Theft Auto is about, it's not difficult to see why the series might face obstacles.

Reuters reports that the Grand Theft Auto franchise has never received official approval for sale in mainland China. GTA 6 is also missing from the regulator's published lists of approved imported games. That's the key point here. It's not a new announcement that the game has been banned outright, but rather that it lacks the approval required for an official domestic release.

A social media promotion doesn't mean GTA 6 has been approved for official sale in mainland China.

The contrast is particularly striking because Rockstar is treating GTA 6 as a worldwide event. The game launched on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and its marketing has reached far beyond the countries where ordinary retail sales are available.

Of course, an official sales restriction doesn't necessarily stop people from playing the game. Reuters says Chinese players have been using foreign console accounts or buying imported boxed editions that include download codes. One Douyin user who said he was in Beijing posted about obtaining a Hong Kong edition for roughly 500 yuan, or about $75.

That doesn't make those purchases part of an officially approved Chinese distribution channel. It simply shows that a market can exist for a game even when the usual local release process isn't available.

It's also worth distinguishing China's situation from the ratings concerns seen in other territories. GTA 6 almost ran into trouble in South Korea, but the issue in mainland China concerns the separate approval system for imported games. They aren't interchangeable cases.

For now, Rockstar can speak to a substantial Chinese audience while GTA 6 remains unavailable for officially approved domestic sales. Whether that situation changes is something only a later regulatory decision could settle. Until then, its Douyin account is a reminder that the game's reach doesn't end at the borders of its official markets.

Strauss Zelnick explained that, while a show or movie isn't impossible, it can only happen if the creative team is 100% on board.

#4233. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

#4226. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

From a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was important that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

In both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

Wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

After the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

After the game launched, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

As a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

For resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel important for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that quickly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

The last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

Wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#4225. 5 new mobile games to try this week - November 19th, 2026

Fresh mobile picks you should give a go this week

Who doesn't love new games? We certainly do - there's just something about the exhilaration of a new title you can't wait to dive into, as the loading screen pops up and you enter a brave new world.

Of course, new mobile games are a dime a dozen these days, and who has the time to scour the iPhone, iPad and/or Android stores to catch the latest title that drops? Fret not - we've gathered a quick list of 5 new mobile games you should try this week, whether that's an undiscovered indie gem or a high-profile AAA masterpiece.

That said, you can head on over to our NEW WEEKLY MOBILE GAMES hub if you're on the hunt for more curated adventures to obsess over!

For me, management sims always have that inevitable level of stress that just gets worse and worse as you progress. Thrifty Business, however, seems to subvert all that, as while you're tasked with managing your own thrift shop, it supposedly does so in a totally chill, totally low-pressure way.

That alone is enough to pique my interest, to be honest, but couple that with its charming visuals and 90s-inspired aesthetics and I'm sold. The sim lets you unlock furniture and decor as you go along, with over 500 cosmetic items you can tinker around with - and the best part of it all is that the first 60 minutes are free for you to try!

My little 12-year-old niece is, I feel, the smartest kid in the world, but even she's not capable of throwing people to the dungeons to keep her kingdom's affairs in order. In Lil' Guardsman, the eponymous Lil is tasked with exactly that, as she's left on gate guard duty by her dear ol' dad. What's doubly more adorable here is that she'll have to deal with all manner of creatures from goblins to elves, and even might have to deal with - god forbid - humans!

It's essentially a border control sim, but with fantasy shenanigans you'll need to investigate throughout your shift. There are more than a hundred different characters whose fates you'll tangle and untangle, so you'd best get your deduction skills on point.

We've got another roguelike in our list this week, and I'm not complaining! Rogue Adventure is a dungeon-crawling RPG with procedurally generated elements where you combine cards and unleash epic skills onto unwitting foes to win.

The turn-based deck-builder features over 15 different classes you can experiment with across four modes, and if you're feeling a little competitive, you can even duke it out with other players in tournaments that refresh every week. The many, many card combos take centre stage here, of course, so suffice it to say you're spoilt for choice.

With the PUBG live-action adaptation having just been announced, everyone's probably looking for ways to dive into the battle royale either as a complete newbie or as a returning veteran just to refresh their shooting skills. Which is why I think PUBG Mobile Flash comes at just the right time, offering all of us a lightweight alternative to dominating Erangel.

The keyword here is "lightweight", with a smaller download size of under 0.96 GB on Android (that's under 1.75 GB on iOS). It's no secret that games are getting heftier and heftier these days, so having something like this in your back pocket with the same optimised experience is definitely a godsend. You can choose what you download, so the maps and modes are available on an "as needed" basis.

Bart Bonte is at it again with his series of colour-themed puzzlers, and this time, it's Brown that's taking the spotlight.

At its core, Bonte's puzzles are all about filling the entire screen with whatever colour's in the title, so for this one, you'll need to do just that across 50 levels. Some puzzles are a simple matter of putting two and two together, while others need a little bit more logic to figure out - thankfully, there's a handy hint system to help you out in case you ever get stuck!

#4224. Ocarina of Time Remake Lets You Pull Off Lynel Trickshots Without Any Lynels

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If there's one thing The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom have taught us, it's that players will eventually find a way to turn even the simplest combat encounter into an opportunity for an unnecessarily impressive trickshot.

Apparently, that mindset isn't going anywhere, even when you take away the open-world freedom of those games, even when we are talking about a more contained gameplay like Ocarina of Time Remake.

A Japanese player recently shared an incredible clip of their own in the newest version of Ocarina of Time, taking down four ReDeads with only four carefully aimed Light Arrows!

Those who have played the original Ocarina of TIme have made quite a number of mistakes after jumping into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

Instead of shooting directly at the enemies, Adult Link fires his arrow high into the sky, letting it travel through the air before hitting all four targets in sequence. The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course. Here, check it out:

The clip takes place in the destroyed Hyrule Market, just before the entrance to Ganon's Castle. It's already an impressive display of precision, but what makes it even better is how unnecessary the whole thing is. Link could probably deal with those ReDeads in a much simpler way. But where's the fun in that?

After its publication, the video quickly gained attention on social media, surpassing 750,000 views and 16,000 likes as we speak! Naturally, other Zelda fans were quick to praise the player's ridiculous display of skill, with one commenter calling it "one of the most impressive things I have ever seen," adding that the precision was an "absolute master class."

Zelda Notes statistics reveal that the most common causes of death are surprisingly embarrassing.

Another player was equally impressed, writing, "Single-handedly the most impressive Zelda clip I ever seen." And honestly, it's hard to disagree! Pulling off a trickshot like this requires a surprising amount of patience and precision, especially when you're trying to hit multiple enemies with an arrow that wasn't even aimed directly at them.

The result looks remarkably similar to the famous Lynel trickshots players have been pulling off in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom – but without any Lynel, of course.

What's particularly fun about this discovery is how it shows that the spirit of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom lives on even in a much more structured adventure. Ocarina of Time doesn't offer the same level of freedom when it comes to approaching combat, but that hasn't stopped players from experimenting with its mechanics and finding creative ways to play.

The more recent games taught an entire generation of Zelda fans that almost every situation can become a playground if you're willing to experiment enough. Whether that's launching enemies into the air, using physics to solve problems in unexpected ways, creating weird machines, or spending far too long trying to land the perfect arrow, players have learned to make their own fun! And now, even without a single Lynel around, that same energy has found its way into Ocarina of Time. I guess some habits really do follow you from one Hyrule to another.

A tapestry hidden in Ocarina of Time's remake depicts Link's journey before it begins, sparking fan theories about Zelda lore and future games.

#4222. Holiday Gift Guide 2026

With the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50

If you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The new Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some users with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25

Many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but currently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059

Many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200

#4220. Cover Reveal – Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis

Game Informer’s next cover story is Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, the upcoming reimagining of the original 1996 Tomb Raider arriving on February 12. Since that game celebrates the franchise’s 30th anniversary this year, we’re doing the same with a double-whammy of Tomb Raider features.

We visited Crystal Dynamics’ office to play Legacy of Atlantis for several hours, including an exclusive tour of the Greece section. For our 12-page cover story, we spoke to key team members at Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog to learn why it’s tackling Lara Croft’s seminal adventure once again (having already remade the game once in Tomb Raider: Anniversary), how this version of the game differs from previous incarnations and why, discuss the teams' controversial use of AI development tools, and how Legacy of Atlantis plants seeds for the upcoming Tomb Raider: Catalyst.

The issue also includes a six-page retrospective of Tomb Raider’s 30-year history, with insights from Crystal Dynamics. This celebration is reflected in our cover art, designed by Tomb Raider franchise art director Brenoch Adams, which showcases every version of Lara Croft from the Core Design, Legend, Survivor, and current eras.

The December issue also marks the return of our annual (and very large) holiday buyers guide, featuring curated gift suggestions for the gamers in your life ahead of the winter holidays. Furthermore, we’ve created a list of family-friendly games to enjoy with younger relatives during upcoming holiday gatherings. Guest contributor Veerender Singh Jubbal writes about India's emerging game development scene and how its community is helping elevate local titles to an international stage. Ahead of the launch of Ryu Ga Gatoku’s Stranger Than Heaven, executive editor Brian Shea played a new section of the era-spanning Yakuza/Like a Dragon prequel while picking the brains of its lead designers for details on the game’s plot, themes, and time periods. #4219. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.
